# The constitution: what an ultrastable system is

> Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.

Read this first. It is generated from `doctrine/constitution.json`, which the system reads at boot and checks against its own code, so nothing here has to be told to the system by a person.

## Identity

An ultrastable system in Ashby's sense (Design for a Brain, 1952): a system that keeps its essential variables inside limits in an environment it cannot predict, by a first loop that acts every tick and a second loop that, when the first cannot hold the variables, changes the first loop's own parameters in discrete steps until it can. Here the first loop is the tick, and the second loop is the goals step and the ladder.

Essential variables (kept inside limits):

- `heartbeat`: every tick step completes, no slot missed
- `k_eff`: k_eff >= k_min over the window
- `silent_drops`: 0 items leave the active set without a disposition
- `metrics_in_breach`: every breach files its own remedy and closes by its probe
- `cost`: spend inside the declared monthly cap
- `unattended_horizon`: simulated horizon p10 >= target_days (365)

Adaptation is discrete and reversible: a knob moves one step within bounds, the effect is predicted, reviewed after review_h, and reverted when the goal did not move. Nothing is tuned continuously or by hand.

## How it runs

One heartbeat on a server-side clock. Each tick: reconcile state, read every metric, score predictions, accrue trust, audit failure modes against their detectors, dispatch work, execute it, measure criticality, record. A failed step is logged and becomes an item; the remaining steps still run.

Tick steps, in order:

1. `reconcile`: every item that left the active set has a disposition (no silent drop)
2. `reap_claims`: claims with no heartbeat are released so work never stalls
3. `connector_health`: every credential is read; a failing refresh becomes one reconnect link, never an instruction
4. `probe_gates`: an identity-bound card closes when its probe passes, and its default stays in effect meanwhile
5. `measure`: every metric is read; a breach files BREACH-<metric> with a closing probe
6. `score_predictions`: each logged prediction is graded against the measured outcome
7. `accrue_trust`: trust per (surface, action class) moves with verified outcomes
8. `selfaudit`: every failure mode in autonomy/failure-modes.json is probed; red files FM-<id>
9. `migrate`: schema migrations apply in order, once
10. `goals`: goals are measured and at most one knob moves one step per cooldown
11. `plan`: the goal furthest out of bounds is broken into small items (audit, implement, verify, fix, integrate, gate) and read again after review_h
12. `unknowns`: the system asks itself what it does not know and files the answer as work
13. `dispatch`: ready items go to the role that owns them
14. `execute`: claimed items are worked, opened as pull requests and merged by the server
15. `check_plus_share`: a share of capacity goes to improvements
16. `age_sla`: an item past its SLA is escalated, never ignored
17. `cost_probe`: spend is sampled against the budget
18. `second_goal`: an objective measured only by its own target is filed; a breached guard under a healthy target is repaired first
19. `criticality`: k_eff is computed from verified deploys over cost and human touches
20. `pulse`: the system publishes what it did, from its own tables
21. `ignition`: the system reads its own stage from bootstrap to self-sustaining

Detectors: every failure mode has a read-only probe (1 = healthy); a red probe files FM-<id> that closes only when the probe is green.
Executor: work is taken in driver order, built on a branch, opened as a pull request and merged by the server when its checks are green; a client session only produces.
Release cadence: every system ships something visible at least weekly; past its cadence the producers are dispatched, past twice the cadence a STALL item is filed.
Changes feed: what the system changed is published from merged work, never typed by hand.

## How it bootstraps

From a bare idea (IDEA.md) to a running, measured, self-improving organization, with no step a person must perform. The boot never dies: a blocked stage is logged, becomes a backlog item with a closing probe, and the next stage runs degraded.

Stages: `read` > `constitute` > `qualify` > `instrument` > `detect` > `select` > `cases` > `plan` > `write` > `surfaces` > `org` > `provision` > `start` > `year_gate` > `verify_live`.

## How it becomes autonomous

Autonomy is earned per (surface, action class) from verified outcomes, never granted by instruction. Trust widens only the system's own loop scopes and acts by pull request; it never widens harness permissions, secrets or the interrupt gate.

Rungs: observed > assisted > delegated > autonomous > self-directed > self-modifying > self-extending.

Ignition stages (read by the system from its own tables): unseeded > seeded > ticking > looping > closing > instrumented > critical > self-sustaining. Bootstrapped from `instrumented`; criticality is the two stages above that.

## Criticality

Criticality is the point where the loop sustains itself: each closed item yields about one new valid item (the branching ratio near 1), verified deploys exceed what they cost in spend and human attention, and no person is on the critical path except an identity-bound gate. It is measured by the system from its own tables; it is never declared.

- `k_eff` >= k_min
- `branching_ratio` between [0.8, 1.2]
- `human_touches` == 0
- `open_ignition_gaps` == 0
- `predictions_scored` >= 1
- `yearsim_horizon_p10_days` >= 365

When below: the first unmet stage is filed as IGNITE-<stage> with the numbers that block it and is closed only by the same reading; the executor's queue narrows to items that raise k_eff.

## Standing rules

Each rule has a detector that sees it break and a remediation that repairs it, both code. A rule with none fails CI.

- **claims-are-code** (Rowan, 2026-11-17): Every statement on a public surface is true because code makes it true, and code checks it on every change.
  - detector: `scripts/claims.py`, `doctrine/claims.json`
  - remediation: `scripts/claims.py`
- **no-static-content** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): Static content is not autonomous. Every page, number and entry is generated and refreshed by a live loop; a page whose text has not changed inside its window is a finding bound to a loop.
  - detector: `scripts/staticcontent.py`, `doctrine/static-content.json` (platform)
  - remediation: `scripts/staticcontent.py`
- **no-waiting-on-owner** (Rowan, 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-21): Nothing waits on a person. An identity-bound act is one machine-readable gate with a default in effect and a closing probe, never an instruction. A blocker is routed around, built, or delegated.
  - detector: `autonomy/failure-modes.json`, `doctrine/standing-order.json`
  - remediation: `worker/src/selfaudit.js`, `autonomy/policy.json`
- **no-owner-secrets** (Rowan, 2026-11-13, 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-20): The owner never handles a credential. Credentials arrive through a consent link and the system stores, refreshes and probes them; a missing one is acquired on every surface, then staged on its default.
  - detector: `worker/src/tick.js`, `doctrine/bootproof.json` (platform)
  - remediation: `worker/src/tick.js`, `bootstrap/platform_github_cloudflare.py`
- **live-verification-before-done** (Rowan, 2026-11-21): Done means observed live by an independent path. A deploy counts only with a probe the changing loop did not write; a report of done without that evidence is a failure mode.
  - detector: `autonomy/failure-modes.json`, `autonomy/criticality.json`
  - remediation: `bootstrap/bootstrap.py`, `worker/src/selfaudit.js`
- **generic-core-vs-tenant** (Rowan, 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-17): Generic capability lives in the core, tenant-agnostic; tenant specifics live only in the tenant. A tenant uses the core through a defined interface and never shares its names, bindings, secrets or data. Improving one system improves every system.
  - detector: `worker/src/tenant.js`, `worker/test/goals.test.js::tenant`
  - remediation: `worker/src/vendor`, `doctrine/tenant-repos.json` (platform)
- **one-year-unattended** (Rowan, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21): The system runs a minimum of one year with no outside input: it prices its cost, repairs its own failures, keeps improving and keeps shipping. The year is simulated, with every declared fault drilled against real recovery code, and a boot whose horizon falls short is refused.
  - detector: `scripts/yearsim.py`, `autonomy/yearsim.json`
  - remediation: `bootstrap/bootstrap.py`, `scripts/seedlife.py`
- **server-side-only** (Rowan, 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13): Every loop, merge, deploy and check runs on infrastructure the system itself runs on (the Worker, its database, the code host's built-in runner). A client session only produces work; the server owns the loop after the pull request opens.
  - detector: `worker/src/handoff.js`, `worker/src/sweeper.js`
  - remediation: `worker/src/lane.js`, `worker/src/sweeper.js`
- **no-silent-drop** (Rowan, 2026-11-12): Every item that enters leaves only with a disposition: entered = open + closed + superseded. An imbalance is an incident.
  - detector: `autonomy/failure-modes.json`, `autonomy/goals.json`
  - remediation: `worker/src/tick.js`
- **code-is-the-only-memory** (Rowan, 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-16): Chat, sessions, reports and tool memory are never storage. Every decision, instruction and standing rule lives in code and data the system consumes, and a session writes back before it ends.
  - detector: `scripts/check_memory.py`, `doctrine/standing-order.json`
  - remediation: `scripts/check_memory.py`, `doctrine/standing-order.json`
- **green-before-merge** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): A server-side merge waits for real, finished, green checks: an empty or still-queued check list is not green.
  - detector: `worker/src/greenguard.js`, `worker/test/health-ignition.test.js::ignition`
  - remediation: `worker/src/lane.js`
- **criticality-measured-not-declared** (Rowan, 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14): Autonomy and criticality are computed by the system from its own tables every tick (k_eff, branching ratio, human touches, ignition gaps). The first unmet stage files its own item and only the same reading closes it. A stage is never declared.
  - detector: `worker/src/ignition.js`, `worker/src/criticality.js`
  - remediation: `worker/src/criticality.js`, `worker/src/goals.js`
- **always-improving** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): The system never runs out of work: each pass files reach, impact, front-end and back-end items and a protected plus slot, and a change is kept only if its metric moved.
  - detector: `scripts/improve.py`, `autonomy/improve.json`
  - remediation: `worker/src/pr-executor.js`, `worker/src/executor.js`
- **every-failure-mode-has-a-detector** (Rowan, 2026-11-21 and 2026-11-25): Every failure mode has a live probe, a failed probe files its own item, and the item closes only when the probe is green; a finding written where no loop reads it is itself a failure mode.
  - detector: `autonomy/failure-modes.json`, `worker/src/selfaudit.js`
  - remediation: `worker/src/selfaudit.js`, `worker/src/selfaudit.js`
- **cold-start-contract** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): Every system is born with the cold-start contract: the same capabilities, each carried by seed files and checked, so nothing a new system needs is supplied by a person afterwards. The constitution adds the rules, ladder and criticality conditions on top of that definition.
  - detector: `doctrine/SYSTEM.md`, `doctrine/coldstart.json` (platform)
  - remediation: `bootstrap/bootstrap.py`, `foundation/coldstart.py` (platform)
- **configs-have-schemas** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): Every JSON config the system runs on has a JSON Schema 2020-12 contract in a Schema Store catalog, generated with the config, so any tool or agent validates it without reading the code that consumes it. The constitution is itself such a config.
  - detector: `doctrine/schemas/catalog.json`, `foundation/configschema.py` (platform)
  - remediation: `doctrine/schemas/constitution.schema.json`, `foundation/configschema.py` (platform)
- **blind-spots-are-measured** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): A reading that is empty is unmeasured, never zero: cost, database growth, credential expiry and published content are each read by a probe, and a probe that cannot read files its own item instead of passing.
  - detector: `worker/src/costsample.js`, `worker/src/tick.js`, `worker/src/apprepos.js`
  - remediation: `worker/src/tick.js`, `worker/src/tick.js`
- **one-contract-front-to-back** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): Every system serves the same public surfaces and declares each statement once, with the page that shows it and the endpoint that backs it; the system's own tests read it front to back and back to front, and its repository says where the code runs.
  - detector: `worker/src/contract.js`, `worker/test/contract.test.js`
  - remediation: `worker/src/discover.js`, `foundation/fleetcontract.py` (platform)
- **one-repository-standard** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): Every repository is held to one standard from the code path that creates it: merge rules, branch cleanup, visibility, one manifest valid against the system schema, and every surface that says what the system is rendered from that manifest. A person who copies the template only states the idea.
  - detector: `scripts/surfaces.py`, `standards/system.schema.json`
  - remediation: `worker/src/repostandard.js`, `scripts/branch_cleanup.py`
- **every-manager-runs** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): Every manager is a running loop that owns code. The managers a system runs are one register, all on by default; the tick hires any switched-on manager with no runtime row and skips one that is switched off with a reason.
  - detector: `autonomy/managers.json`, `worker/test/managers.test.js`
  - remediation: `worker/src/managers.js`, `foundation/managers.py` (platform)
- **open-standards** (Rowan, 2026-11-25): Every format the system runs on is an established open standard registered in doctrine/open-standards.json (JSON Schema for config, CloudEvents for event ledgers, OpenAPI for HTTP, Wrangler for infrastructure, Atom and JSON Feed for feeds, MCP and AGENTS.md for agents, and registered planned rows for the rest), a new bespoke format fails CI, and the baseline of older files drains by a daily loop.
  - detector: `scripts/openstd.py`, `foundation/openstd.py` (platform)
  - remediation: `scripts/openstd.py`, `foundation/openstd.py` (platform)
- **one-work-record** (Rowan, 2026-11-26): Every request and every task a session or loop starts has one server-side work record (goal, owner, state, done check, PRs, next step, heartbeat) outside any chat or session; a record whose owner goes silent is handed back to the server lane to resume from its next step.
  - detector: `agents/AGENTS.md`, `foundation/worklog.py` (platform)
  - remediation: `agents/AGENTS.md`, `foundation/worklog.py` (platform)
- **phased-large-change** (Rowan, 2026-11-26): Any change too large for one author runs one phased shape: audit, coverage, implement, verify by an evidence and an adversarial reader who did not write it, fix only what was found, integrate, and a final gate on the whole change. The shape is data a session, a workflow or the Worker all follow.
  - detector: `autonomy/phases.json`, `worker/src/orchestrate.js`
  - remediation: `scripts/phasework.py`, `worker/src/orchestrate.js`
- **every-essential-variable-holds-a-veto** (Rowan, 2026-11-27): A change the second loop makes is judged by every essential variable, not only the one it was made for: a step that knocks a variable that was holding out of its limits is undone, and the undo is read as a trial. The search for a value that holds goes on past a knob's declared direction, and the regulator reads its own variety and structure from its own tables. The mechanisms are taken from W. Ross Ashby's journal and cite its pages.
  - detector: `worker/src/ashby.js`, `worker/src/regulation.js`
  - remediation: `worker/src/goals.js`, `worker/src/ashby.js`
- **second-goal-in-code** (Rowan, 2026-11-27): The explicit goal is subordinate to the essential variables. Every objective with a target carries a guard its target does not move; a breached guard under a healthy target is repaired before the goal is pursued; a step is drawn only from untried, reversible candidates and kept only when the variables held; a task that harms the one who does it is not prescribed, and past failures are always recalled.
  - detector: `worker/src/secondloop.js`, `autonomy/secondloop.json`
  - remediation: `worker/src/secondloop.js`, `worker/src/organization.js`
- **automation-never-discards-work** (Rowan, 2026-11-27): Automation never closes a pull request on a label, a cached state or an unknown state: it reads the pull request live, tries to update its branch, and pins the head under refs/archive before any close. A pull request automation closed that main still lacks is reopened.
  - detector: `worker/src/prsafe.js`
  - remediation: `worker/src/prsafe.js`, `worker/src/sweeper.js`
